key_cases.case_name: Commonwealth, Cabinet for Health & Family Services v. C.V.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of the Cabinet's termination petition because the circuit court made no findings that would support termination, while agreeing with the Cabinet that a district-court change of the permanency goal from reunification to adoption is not a prerequisite to filing a termination petition.
key_cases.relevance: This is Kentucky's published example of a termination petition properly dismissed for want of findings, with leave to refile.
key_cases.quote: Under KRS 625.090(3)(c), the court can make its own concurrent finding as to reasonable efforts

key_cases.holding: The court vacated an abuse-and-neglect adjudication because the family court failed to decide the truth or falsity of the petition's allegations under KRS 620.100(3), relied on evidence outside the record, and used the DNA hearing to resolve custody.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion explains that unproven allegations require a ruling in the parent's favor rather than a custody disposition.
key_cases.quote: The family court did not follow the statutory requirement that it determine the truth or falsity of the allegations in the complaint

key_cases.case_name: Commonwealth, Cabinet for Health & Family Services ex rel. M.H. v. R.H.
key_cases.holding: The court held that issue preclusion did not bar the Cabinet from introducing evidence identifying a parent as the perpetrator of prior sexual abuse of the child's seven siblings, because the earlier court had not actually decided the perpetrator's identity and that identity is not material to a finding that a parent created a risk of sexual abuse; it vacated the dismissal and ordered an expedited adjudication.
key_cases.relevance: The court vacated a dismissal that had been entered after the family court excluded the sibling-abuse evidence, showing that evidentiary error cannot be the basis for closing a case.
key_cases.quote: The identity of the perpetrator of the abuse is not material to that finding.
